Note::TexAccessor::env¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::env(std::string_view name) const

Extract One Environment Kind¶

env() returns complete \begin{name}...\end{name} regions for one requested environment. Use it when the environment kind is known and the full authored region, including delimiters, must survive. Unlike env_names(), it requires a closing command; unlike envs(), it excludes every other environment kind.

Matching is exact and case-sensitive. proof does not select proof*, while align* can be requested directly. The parser balances nested regions with the same name, so an inner proof belongs to its outer proof token rather than prematurely ending it. Different nested environment kinds are simply content. Doubled-backslash text is not treated as an opener, and an incomplete outer region produces no partial token.

Multiple non-overlapping matches in one cell are emitted in source order. tokens() contains the complete regions and offsets() retains cell ownership, including empty lanes. This is the canonical generic operation; there are deliberately no per-environment aliases.

name accepts letters and @, plus an optional final *; it must not include a leading backslash or braces. Invalid names throw. Undefined input returns an undefined token Note with offsets [0], and non-text input is rejected. The balanced scan is linear and copies only matched regions.

Example 1: Balance A Nested Environment¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\begin{proof}outer \begin{proof}inner\end{proof} tail\end{proof})",
    R"(\begin{lemma}other\end{lemma})", R"(\begin{proof}unfinished)",
    R"(\\begin{proof}escaped\end{proof})"});
const auto proofs = source.tex().env("proof");
std::cout << proofs.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{proof}outer \\begin{proof}inner\\end{proof} tail\\end{proof}"]

Example 2: Empty Lanes Remain Addressable¶

const auto offsets = proofs.offsets().integers();
std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 1, 1, 1, 1]

Only cell zero owns a match. The lemma, incomplete proof, and escaped opener do not become proof tokens.

Example 3: Reject A Malformed Name¶

try { (void)source.tex().env("bad name"); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "env(bad name): rejected\n"; }

Output¶

env(bad name): rejected

See Also¶

  • env_names: inventory openers, including incomplete ones.

  • envs: return all complete environment kinds.

  • align_blocks: select both align spellings semantically.
